question: Nearly shared: prediction of MCI progression to AD from structural T1 MRI in ADNI. P-3 (Luo et al., Comput Biol Med 2023): 295 pMCI (dementia within 36 months) vs 298 sMCI (still MCI), whole 3D T1 volumes, 5-fold CV on the Wen et al. splits. P-41 (Rahim et al., Image Vis Comput 2025): 96 sMCI (MCI from baseline to M48) vs a positive class of 81 pMCI (conversion between M18 and M48) plus 15 patients with established AD, 132 2D slices per plane from three planes, one 15 + 15 subject test set. Input representation, architecture, horizon window, sample size and validation differ, which the rule allows. The open point is the positive class: about one in six of P-41's positives (15/96) are not MCI at all, so its task is partly stable MCI against dementia.
metric: Accuracy with accuracy (74.61% vs 91.77%) and ROC-AUC with ROC-AUC (0.780 vs 0.9287).

figures.P-3: CAAT ensemble, 5-fold CV over 593 subjects (295 pMCI / 298 sMCI): accuracy 74.61% and AUC 0.780, with fold variances (0.002, 0.003) and no interval. Wilson for accuracy (n = 593): centre (0.7461 + 1.9208/593)/(1 + 3.8416/593) = 0.745, half-width 0.035, CI [0.710, 0.780]. Hanley-McNeil for AUC with 295/298: Q1 = 0.78/1.22 = 0.6393, Q2 = 2(0.78^2)/1.78 = 0.6836, SE = 0.0190, CI [0.743, 0.817].
figures.P-41: Best configuration (EN + CN + DN ensemble, CBAM, MHA head) on the 30-subject test set (15 sMCI / 15 pMCI-or-AD): accuracy 91.77% +/- 3.14, sensitivity 87.69% +/- 3.24, specificity 88.53% +/- 3.53, AUC 92.87% +/- 3.58 (+/- are run SDs, not intervals). Wilson for 0.9177 at n = 30: centre (0.9177 + 0.0640)/1.128 = 0.870, half-width 0.104, CI [0.766, 0.974]. On a balanced 15/15 test set accuracy must equal (sensitivity + specificity)/2 = 0.881, not 0.9177; Wilson for 0.881 at n = 30: CI [0.721, 0.955]. Hanley-McNeil for AUC 0.9287 with 15/15: Q1 = 0.9287/1.0713 = 0.8669, Q2 = 2(0.9287^2)/1.9287 = 0.8944, SE = sqrt([0.9287*0.0713 + 14*(0.8669-0.8625) + 14*(0.8944-0.8625)]/225) = 0.0505, CI [0.830, 1.000].

matched_figure_check: No matched figure. P-41 reports no result with the 15 AD patients removed, no whole-volume 3D input and no 36-month window; all its variants (Experiments 1-3, e.g. DN + DN + DN with an LSTM head at 76.20%) are its own 2D-slice ensembles on the same pMCI-plus-AD test set. P-3 reports no result with AD patients in the positive class. Nothing in either paper closes the gap.
performance_validity: Not excluded by Section 3.5: P-41's 0.9177 accuracy and 0.9287 AUC are below 0.97, although they rest on an internal 30-subject test set with no external cohort. Checked against the source: P-41 reports all results on that test set while comparing many ensemble and head configurations on it, and its printed accuracy is higher than both its sensitivity and its specificity, which a balanced 15/15 test cannot produce. P-3 notes that tuning and selecting on the same 5-fold CV may bias its own estimate upward.

candidate_explanations.difference: Positive class: P-41 adds 15 patients with established AD to its progressive group, so part of its task is separating stable MCI from dementia, which is easier than separating converters from stable MCI.
candidate_explanations.quote: Furthermore, we added 15 pa-tients with AD to the pMCI group to help the model learn both the progressive and fully diseased brain patterns simultaneously.

candidate_explanations.difference: Label windows: P-41's converters convert between M18 and M48 against stability to M48; P-3's convert within 36 months against a diagnosis that stays MCI.
candidate_explanations.quote: The second group (pMCI) included 81 participants who were diagnosed with MCI at baseline but progressed to AD within 2.5 years, between month 18 (M18) and M48.

candidate_explanations.difference: Evaluation-set size and model selection: 30 test subjects, on which P-41 compares its many ensemble and head configurations, against 5-fold CV over 593 subjects.
candidate_explanations.quote: The dataset was carefully partitioned to ensure that no data leakage occurred, and all results reported in this study were based on the test set.

candidate_explanations.difference: Input representation and architecture: multi-plane 2D slice stacks through a heterogeneous CNN ensemble with CBAM and multi-head attention (P-41) vs whole 3D volumes through a 5-layer 3D CNN with attention transferred from AD/CN, ADAS and CDR-SB source tasks (P-3).
candidate_explanations.quote: From each vol-ume, 132 middle slices from the axial, coronal, and sagittal planes were selected

candidate_explanations.difference: Cohort and scanner: P-41 selects 192 ADNI-1/GO/2 subjects on data availability, all 3 T; P-3 uses 593 ADNI-1/2 subjects on the benchmark splits of Wen et al.
candidate_explanations.quote: Our dataset consists of 593 MRI images, consisting of 298 sMCIs and 295 pMCIs images. We performed 5 fold cross validation using the same data splits as that used in [11]

candidate_explanations.difference: Evaluation bias acknowledged by P-3 (which would, if anything, inflate P-3 rather than P-41).
candidate_explanations.quote: A limitation of our experimental setup is the use of 5 fold cross validation for both tuning and selecting the models. This may lead to an optimistically biased evaluation of the model performance.

reason: Everything except the positive class lines up: the same ADNI T1 MRI channel, the same metrics, no matched figure, no figure at the 0.97 ceiling, and AUCs that exclude each other in both directions (0.9287 [0.830, 1.000] vs 0.780 [0.743, 0.817]; z = 0.149/sqrt(0.019^2 + 0.0505^2) = 2.76). The accuracies also exclude each other on the printed 91.77%; on the 88.1% that P-41's own sensitivity and specificity imply, the exclusion holds in one direction only. But P-41 puts 15 patients with established AD into its progressive class, so it measures stable MCI against converters plus dementia. If the operator reads that as a label-definition difference, which the rule lists among candidate explanations, the pair qualifies with the explanations below, none shown to be sufficient. If the operator reads it as a different comparison, the pair fails condition 1.
